text:
Nashville had this one with four minutes left. Mavrik Bourque's goal midway through the third put the Predators up 5-4 and their win chance at 84%. Then Anders Lee scored his second of the afternoon at 16:05, Vincent Trocheck was the only shooter to score in the shootout, and Utah left Bridgestone Arena with a 6-5 win.

It was a strange game to lose on the scoreboard and an easy one to explain on the ice. Utah out-attempted Nashville 78-48, outshot it 35-21 and built 4.01 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 2.26; in replays of every shot, the Mammoth win 77% of the time. Nashville stayed in it by finishing the long ones. Filip Forsberg scored 52 seconds in on a slap shot with a 4% chance, and Roman Josi made it 2-0 shorthanded late in the first. Utah answered with two in the last 87 seconds of the period, Clayton Keller on a backhand and Mikhail Sergachev on a 2% wrist shot with six seconds left, and Lee's first, a 26% chance, gave the Mammoth the lead late in the second.

The third was chaos. Alexander Kerfoot tied it unassisted, Lawson Crouse put Utah back ahead, Ross Colton tied it again 49 seconds later, and Bourque gave Nashville the lead. Lee's tying goal, set up by Dylan Guenther, was the biggest swing of the day, taking Utah from 10% to 48%. Juuse Saros made the save of the game in overtime on Logan Cooley, then stopped everyone but Trocheck in the shootout. Forsberg, Ryan O'Reilly and Josi all came up empty against Karel Vejmelka.

Vejmelka will take the win and not much else: five goals on 21 shots, 2.7 more than those shots deserved. MacKenzie Weegar had three assists. Two days after ending Minnesota's 15-game point streak, Utah came back from two goals down and kept rolling, and the Predators, who had beaten Dallas on Wednesday, let a lead that late slip away, which is the kind of loss that stings for a while.
headline: Anders Lee drags Utah back, Trocheck finishes it
